(Durham, North Carolina) | college = * [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] (2020–2022) * [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2022–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team1 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team2 = →[[Delaware Blue Coats]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team3 = [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2023) * [[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] Sixth Man of the Year ([[2021–22 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|2022]]) * AAC All-Freshman team (2021) }} '''Ricky Nickardo Council IV''' (born August 3, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State Shockers]] and the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. ==Early life== Council grew up in [[Durham, North Carolina]] and attended [[Southern School of Energy and Sustainability]].{{cite web|first=Jacey|last=Zembal|title=Local standout Ricky Council IV hits portal |url=https://ncstate.rivals.com/news/local-standout-ricky-council-iv-hits-portal|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=April 21, 2022|access-date=December 2, 2022}} He was named third-team All-State as a senior after averaging 23 points, 9.5 rebounds, and five assists per game.{{cite web|first=Richard|last=Davenport|title=Hogs get another player from portal|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/may/14/hogs-get-another-player-from-portal/|work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=May 14, 2022|access-date=December 2, 2022}} Council was rated a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] over offers from [[Rice Owls men's basketball|Rice]], [[Appalachian State Mountaineers men's basketball|Appalachian State]], [[Elon Phoenix men's basketball|Elon]], [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra]], [[UMBC Retrievers men's basketball|UMBC]], [[Georgia Southern Eagles men's basketball|Georgia Southern]], [[Siena Saints men's basketball|Siena]], [[James Madison Dukes men's basketball|James Madison]], and [[Coastal Carolina Chanticleers men's basketball|Coastal Carolina]].{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Eldridge|title=Ricky Council IV commits to Wichita State basketball 2020|url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article241608461.html|work=[[The Wichita Eagle]]|date=March 29, 2020|access-date=December 2, 2022}} ==College career== Council began his college career at Wichita State. He averaged 7.1 points and 3.4 rebounds over 21 games and was named to the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) All-Freshman team.{{cite web|first=Richard|last=Davenport|title=Musselman's quick call, communication gets visit from Council|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/may/07/musselmans-quick-call-communication-gets-visit-from-council/|work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=May 7, 2022|access-date=December 2, 2022}} As a sophomore, Council played in all 28 of the Shockers' games with seven starts and averaged 12 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 1.1 steals per game and was named the AAC Sixth Man of the Year.{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=McPherson|title=Arkansas junior wing Ricky Council IV proves wisdom of Muss’ last portal move|url=https://www.nwahomepage.com/sports/pig-trail-nation/arkansas-junior-wing-ricky-council-iv-proves-wisdom-of-muss-last-portal-move/|website=[[KNWA-TV|NWAHomepage.com]]|date=August 22, 2022|access-date=December 2, 2022|archive-date=December 2, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221202162414/https://www.nwahomepage.com/sports/pig-trail-nation/arkansas-junior-wing-ricky-council-iv-proves-wisdom-of-muss-last-portal-move/|url-status=dead}} Following the end of the season, he initially declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Eldridge|title=Wichita State's Ricky Council to test 2022 NBA Draft waters|url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article259840060.html|work=[[The Wichita Eagle]]|date=March 28, 2022|access-date=December 2, 2022}} Council withdrew his name from the draft and entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Eldridge|title=Wichita State's Ricky Council enters NCAA transfer portal|url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article260618227.html|work=[[The Wichita Eagle]]|date=April 21, 2022|access-date=December 2, 2022}} Council committed to transfer to [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].{{cite web|first=Christina|last=Long|title=Arkansas basketball lands Ricky Council IV of Wichita State|url=https://www.swtimes.com/story/sports/college/2022/05/13/ricky-council-transfer-arkansas-basketball-wichita-state-eric-musselman/9719247002/|work=[[Southwest Times Record]]|date=May 13, 2022|access-date=December 2, 2022}} He was named second team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) at the end of his junior season.{{cite web|first=Bob|last=Holt|title=Arkansas' Council named to AP team|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2023/mar/08/arkansas-council-named-to-ap-team/|work=[[The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=March 8, 2023|access-date=March 27, 2023}} Council averaged 16.1 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists, and 1.1 steals per game.{{cite web|first=Mason|last=Choate|title=Ricky Council IV declares for 2023 NBA Draft|url=https://arkansas.rivals.com/news/ricky-council-iv-declares-for-2023-nba-draft|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=April 5, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}} After the conclusion of the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023 NCAA tournament]], he announced that he would forgo the remainder of his college eligibility and enter the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Bob|last=Holt|title=Arkansas' Council declares for draft|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2023/apr/05/arkansas-council-declares-for-draft/|work=[[The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=April 5, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers / Delaware Blue Coats (2023–2025)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Council signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on July 1, 2023.{{cite web|title=Ricky Council IV and Terquavion Smith Signed to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/ricky-council-iv-terquavion-smith-sign-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2023|access-date=October 25, 2023}} Council was waived on October 20,{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Sixers Waive Ricky Council, David Duke Jr.|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/sixers-waive-ricky-council-david-duke-jr.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 25, 2023}} but signed a new two-way contract with the team on October 25.{{cite web|title=Ricky Council IV Signed to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/ricky-council-iv-signed-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2023|access-date=October 26, 2023}} On January 2, 2024, Council made his NBA debut for the 76ers in a 110–97 win over the [[2023–24 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|first=C. Steve|last=Andrews|title=Council IV makes NBA debut with Philadelphia|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/former-hog-standout-council-iv-202432919.html|website=Yahoo.com|date=January 3, 2024|access-date=January 7, 2024}} and on February 10, he had a career-high 19 points and 10 rebounds against the [[2023–24 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]]. On April 13, he signed a standard contract with the 76ers.{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Ricky Council IV to Standard NBA Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-ricky-council-iv-to-standard-nba-contract|website=NBA.com|date=April 13, 2024|access-date=April 13, 2024}} On January 26, 2025, Council was shortly [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] to the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Delaware Blue Coats Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Delaware-Blue-Coats/57/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 27, 2025}} He made 73 appearances (12 starts) for Philadelphia during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 7.3 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. On July 25, Council was waived by the 76ers.{{Cite web|title=Sixers waive Ricky Council IV, open up roster spot|url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/sixers-waive-ricky-council-iv-open-up-roster-spot/676552/?amp=1|access-date=July 30, 2025|website=nbcsportsphiladelphia.com|language=es}} === Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2025–present) === On October 18, 2025, Council signed with the [[Houston Rockets]], but was waived shortly after.{{Cite web |last=Maher |first=Rory |date=October 18, 2025 |title=Rockets Waive Carey, Council, Hunter, Matthews |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/10/rockets-waive-carey-council-hunter-matthews.html |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en-US}} On October 27, 2025, he signed with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web |title=VIPERS ANNOUNCE 2025-26 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER
